mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the empty universe, making AuditOnEveryTransition and AuditImmutable vacuously true because the quantifications over AuditEntry find no witnesses. This demonstrates that the assertions depend on the universe being populated.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonEmptyUniverse { some User and some LoanApplication and some AuditEntry }

mutation_targets.rationale: The one-in-flight assertion requires at least one User to be meaningful. Without it, the predicate is vacuously satisfied.
Role-related invariants require a populated universe to be tested. Removing the fact allows vacuous satisfaction.
Removing the permission matrix definition allows arbitrary role-operation pairs to be added, violating the principle of least privilege.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionViolation { Applicant -> PatchApplicationStatus in PermMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the audit immutability constraint allows an AuditEntry to be modified after creation, directly violating append-only semantics.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMutation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.application = ae2.application and ae1.new_status != ae2.new_status }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this constraint allows self-assignment, violating the no-self-assignment rule from FR-010 and FR-011.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfAssignment { some app: LoanApplication | app.assigned_officer = app.applicant_user }
